title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Balder Knights came to Lordran in large numbers along with their king, Knight King Rendal, seeking a cure for the Undead curse. However, none were able to defeat the Iron Golem, and they ended up as Hollows in the Undead Parish or Sen's Fortress.

It is possible that at least one Balder Knight managed to enter Anor Londo, becoming a member of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Balder Knights are located in the Undead Parish, and Sen's Fortress.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Balder Knights** are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : There are three varieties of Balder Knights: Side Sword, Rapier, and Crossbow. Those wielding rapiers are stronger and drop more souls.

The Rapier variant of the Balder Knight can switch stances, holding its weapon at chest level, pointed at the player. While its stance is altered thus, the Balder Knight can parry.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Several corpses of Balder knights can be found in the Undead Parish and Sen's Fortress, and are the only preplaced corpses in the game to have armor on their dead body.
Their armor has a similar design to the armor worn by Guts, the protagonist of the *Berserk* anime/manga, during its Golden Age arc.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Balder Knights have a fair amount of health, and are a considerable threat to new characters. Even one-on-one, they can be very dangerous.

Any ranged attack is useful against them, but they are fast and will close the gap quickly. Firebombs can be very useful in defeating them.

Critical attacks, such as the Parry and Riposte and Backstab, are exceedingly efficient methods to dispatch these enemies.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Berenike Knights were known for their heavy armor of steel and their ultra-heavy Tower Shields forged with thick plates of iron, favoring hard defense and stability, as well as their gigantic swords capable of causing enormous damage. For their immense strength these knights were extolled as the mightiest of mighty. Among them, Black Iron Tarkus was renowned even among his fellow knights for his great strength; he wore an ultra-heavy armor made of special black iron—one with exceptional fire protection, yet so unwieldy that only he was able to wear it; his greatshield, made of the same fire-resistant material, was even heavier than that of his fellow knights.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Berenike Knights**, also known as **Heavy Knights**, are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Large and clad in the Steel Set, they wield either a large Mace or Greatsword, depending on the location where they are found, along with a Tower Shield. All Berenike Knights can be parried, but cannot be riposted.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Undead Parish — A Berenike Knight Demon can be found near the Undead Church as a miniboss guarding the Fire Keeper Soul.
Sen's Fortress — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.
Painted World of Ariamis — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.

title: Bloathead
snippet:
Bloathead -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Bloatheads are the disturbed remnants of the populace of Oolacile, whose humanity went out of control after the Dark of Manus, father of the Abyss, overtook them.

title: Bloathead
snippet:
Bloathead -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : A Bloathead is killed by Knight Artorias in the intro cinematic before his boss fight.

title: Bloathead
snippet:
Bloathead -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Bloatheads can be found throughout Oolacile Township and the Chasm of the Abyss. One is also located on the elevator in the Oolacile Township Dungeon.

title: Bloathead
snippet:
Bloathead -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Bloatheads** are enemies in *Dark Souls*. They are only found in the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC.

title: Bloathead
snippet:
Bloathead -  Dark Souls - enemy - description

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategies 
 strategies : A good way to fight Blue Drakes is to have a shield that can block at least 80 percent Lightning damage.

Staying in close-quarters with a Blue Drake will trigger its melee attack until the player moves far enough away. Moving behind it can cause it to fly in the air and shower an area of effect Lightning attack. One should also be cautious of straying too far away, as the majority of their attacks exceed their lock-on distance. This can cause players attempting to backpedal out of the way of an attack to spontaneously turn around and cease blocking.

It is safer to fight these creatures one by one in an open area.

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Several can be found in the Valley of Drakes, in front of the sealed gate leading to New Londo Ruins.

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Blue Drakes**, also known as **Drakes** or **Wyverns**, are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - drops 
 drops : Wyverns are the only respawning enemies that drop Dragon Scales, making them the only constant source for this item for offline players.

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : They have blueish indigo scales, are capable of flight, and strongly resemble the Hellkite Dragon, however, Blue Drakes are smaller and breathe Lightning.

title: Blue Drake
snippet:
Blue Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Unlike most dragon-kin enemies, they are highly resistant to lightning damage, but are very weak against fire damage.
The sound they make is identical to the one made by a dragon in *Demon's Souls*.

title: Darkwraith (enemy)
snippet:
Darkwraith (enemy) -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Darkwraiths are one of three enemies that drop Titanite Slabs, the others being Crystal Lizards and the Stray Demon; however, Darkwraiths can respawn, thus being the most reliable source of Titanite Slabs in one playthrough.

title: Darkwraith (enemy)
snippet:
Darkwraith (enemy) -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Darkwraiths were once knights of the Four Kings of New Londo before descending into Dark along with their masters. Provoked by Darkstalker Kaathe, they use the art of Lifedrain, the power of the Dark Soul to absorb Humanity. Their threat grew so large that all of New Londo was flooded, trapping them in the Abyss.

Despite being consistently hostile, it seems that they are all part of the actual Darkwraith covenant, and appear as dark servants in other places besides New Londo.

title: Darkwraith (enemy)
snippet:
Darkwraith (enemy) -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Lower New Londo Ruins, after the water has been drained.

title: Darkwraith (enemy)
snippet:
Darkwraith (enemy) -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Darkwraiths** are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Usage of the Dragon Eye is limited to players who are members of the Path of the Dragon covenant.

Using the Dragon Eye causes the player's sign to appear in the worlds of other players, allowing them to summon the user to their world to duel. The player does not need to be in human form. However, the host must be in human form (reverse-hollowed), but does not need to possess a Dragon Scale (contrary to the in-game description), and the area boss does not need to be alive to interact with the summon sign; users of the dragon eye have no such restrictions as to where and when they can place their signs. Players can summon others that are within their soul level +/-(10+10%) of their level; for example, a level 100 player can be summoned by anyone between level 80 and 120.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : Obtained after joining the Path of the Dragon covenant.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet: The winner of the duel is granted a Dragon Scale and souls proportional to the defeated player's soul level. In the event of a tie (where both players die), both players are awarded a Dragon Scale. Despite the nature of dragon dueling, the host may indict the Dragon Eye user if they are defeated.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : The **Dragon Eye** is an online play item in *Dark Souls*.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Online play item. Find a player who has acquired a Dragon Scale and invade that player's world to pillage it. (Only Covenanter can use the item).

An art of the transcendent apostles who pray to the ancient dragons. To be alive is to be vulnerable, and the fiery Gods are no exception. The apostles seek another plane of existence, which transcends life.

title: Dragon Scale
snippet:
Dragon Scale -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Dragon Scales can be used to reinforce Dragon weapons and increase one's rank in the Path of the Dragon covenant.

title: Dragon Scale
snippet:
Dragon Scale -  Dark Souls - item - description

A dragon is inseparable from its scales, and the transcendent apostles, who seek the perpetuity of the ancient dragons, have crossed the very end of the earth to seek this invaluable treasure.

title: Giant
snippet:
Giant -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Gigantic humanoids that perform various tasks in Sen's Fortress. They look identical to the Giant Blacksmith and have similar attacks.

Although they share the same name, they share only a few similarities with the Giants in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Giant
snippet:
Giant -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : When fighting a giant, hack away at the legs and dodge any of the giants attacks. This is simple, as their attacks are quite slow. After continuing this rhythm for a short while, eventually the giant will flail around angrily and stomp. This is fairly easy to block with a medium shield and easier to dodge. After the giant has finished its rampage it will crouch down leaving itself defenseless. This is the time that the player should exhaust their entire firepower on the giant.

A safe, although potentially expensive, strategy is to use the Toxic status to kill the Giants. Throwing two Dung Pies at a Giant is enough to apply the effect in NG. After the Toxin takes effect, the player must only wait until the Giant dies.

title: Giant
snippet:
Giant -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Encountered at various points in Sen's Fortress.
The Gatekeeper can be found behind an illusory wall at the top of the ladder leading up from the Titanite Demons.
The Firebomber can be found at the very top of the fortress raining down large firebombs at the player.
The only respawning Giant is the one that drops the spherical boulders that are encountered throughout the Fortress. It can either be shot with a projectile or reached by taking a running leap from the bridge close to where the Crestfallen Merchant resides. As it respawns, and doesn't drop any items, it may be worthwhile to simply ignore it.

title: Giant
snippet:
Giant -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead

title: Giant Clam
snippet:
Giant Clam -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Giant Clams are an easy source of Twinkling Titanite, an otherwise expensive upgrade material. They can be farmed in Ash Lake and the Crystal Cave, where they can be respawned repeatedly.
Shooting an arrow into a Giant Clam's mouth will briefly stun it.
When encountering Seath the Scaleless for the first time, in the Crystal Cave, the fog wall is not present. This allows the clams the chance to enter the room that houses the boss fight, if the player tries to run past them. Seath's attacks can harm them, but they will still only attack the player, making the fight a fair bit more challenging.

While not particularly powerful, Giant Clams have plenty of attacks performed in quick succession that can knock the player off their feet, effectively stun-locking the player to death. This becomes much more evident when they attack in groups.

title: Giant Leech

title: Giant Leech
snippet:

 description : Giant Leeches are somewhat passive creatures, some not even bothering to attack the player unless they do so first. They navigate through the poison slowly and can charge at the player or spit at them with poison globules.

Unless a large number of them charge the player all at once, their potential danger to the player is minimal.

title: Giant Leech

title: Guardian
snippet:
Guardian -  Dark Souls - enemy - note 
 note : After performing a ground smash, Guardians sometimes look around for the player, leaving them vulnerable to a few free hits. However, the Guardian can pull its axe out of the ground with a big explosion if the player is within range for too long.
Guardians strongly resemble Stone Knights. Their armor is quite similar and they both guard forests.

title: Guardian

Guardian -  Dark Souls - enemy - description

title: Guardian

Extremely high Slash defense
Medium Normal and Thrust defense
Low Strike defense

title: Gyrm
snippet:
Gyrm -  Dark Souls II - enemy - description 
 description : A stocky, powerful race which once dwelt aboveground, they were regarded as inferior by humans and unjustly exiled below. They are amicable by nature but harbor an intense distrust of surface dwellers, particularly humans; in additions many of the Gyrm living in the Doors of Pharros have gone Hollow and become threats to the living.

 strategy : Although small, the Gyrm fight with vicious force. They wield flails that they swing like whips and can combo up to three swings in a row. Due to their small size, they can be easily stun-locked. This can be used to gain a significant advantage over them.

They are often found in a sitting position, facing away from the player's path. This, combined with their poor hearing, makes them very susceptible to backstabs.

title: Gyrm

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - darkroot_basin 
 darkroot_basin : The Darkroot Basin Hydra rests in a deep pit beyond an otherwise shallow pond and hardly moves at all. By wearing the Rusted Iron Ring, mobility will not be an issue throughout the fight, although care should be taken not to walk too far into the lake, risking a sudden death by sinking into deep water, whether by human mistake, by being pulled in by one of the Hydra's heads while it is retracting, or by being launched in by the area of effect blast unleashed by the water projectiles.

Crystal Golems in the area can be damaged by the Hydra's water projectiles.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Crystal Golems in the area can be damaged by the Hydra's water projectiles.

As the player approaches the Hydra at a distance from its front, the slightly elevated area on the left, from the player's perspective, is almost completely safe from the water projectiles; however, they are relatively easy to block. Although the player is relatively safe from health and stamina damage when blocking, the water projectiles can still deal substantial stamina damage through the shield. Alternatively, equipping the Ring of Fog will allow the player to approach the Hydra much closer. The monster will still start shooting projectiles, although at no specific direction until the player gets too near.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The Hydra can be defeated by severing its heads or by targeting the main body and using ranged attacks.

As the player moves closer to the shore, the Hydra will almost exclusively use its head strikes. After it lunges toward the player, each head will bury itself in the ground for a short time, presenting an opportunity to sever its vulnerable necks. As each head is defeated, the spread of the Hydra's attacks will diminish, making it easier for the player to finish the job.

The lunge attacks can be blocked or dodged. Certain spots can be found where the heads will completely miss the player. If the Hydra's position does not change, these spots can be exploited throughout the battle.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : A Hydra can be found at the bottom of Darkroot Basin and another is found close to the entrance to Ash Lake.

title: Hydra
snippet: For melee based characters, one of the major dangers while confronting the Hydra is actually reaching a distance where it starts lunging, as that means having to evade or block the constant barrage of homing water shots. Wearing the Ring of Fog allows the player to approach the Hydra without issues, to the point that it will only become hostile once the player is right in front of it, having a melee based fight for the most part from the beginning. Unlike the Hydra fight in Darkroot Basin, the waters of the shore where this battle takes place is shallow, so the Rusted Iron Ring is not necessary for this fight.

title: Hydra
snippet: While using a hit and run method, players can utilize the rock and tree near the edge of the water as cover from the water projectiles and head strikes. After the Hydra thrusts its heads into the ground, hack at one of the necks until the head is severed. Each head will land in the same relative position after every attack. The heads that land closest to the player will normally be chopped off first, while the last head will be very hard to hit with melee attacks. Because the remaining head will always miss the player even when standing still, this head can be safely dispatched with ranged attacks. A few shots will quickly sever the head and defeat the Hydra. Alternatively, the last head can be reached with close range weapons if the Hydra's position is shifted by running along the water's edge, or if the player starts running towards its landing spot the moment the attack is initiated.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Since they drop Dragon Scales when defeated, the Hydras could possibly be descendants of the Everlasting Dragons.
In Greek mythology, the Hydra was a serpent-like, multi-headed water beast. Various accounts of the creature claim that for each head that was severed, one to multiple more would sprout in its place.

title: Hydra
snippet:
When moving closer toward the Hydra in Darkroot Basin, tilting the camera higher will help identify the dark areas from the shallow side. Venturing into the deep end will cause the player to abruptly sink, as one would fall from a cliff, resulting in an instant death.
It is possible to shoot off the Hydra's heads from Darkroot Garden, though it may require many arrows and a long range bow. The Black Bow of Pharis makes a good choice for this, if the player has the stats to wield it, as it can be found on the way to the pass overlooking the Hydra. May require the Hawk Ring for further range. The last head must be attacked directly with a weapon to kill it.
Resting at a bonfire will cause the Hydra to regenerate its lost health, but any heads which have been severed will remain that way.
The Hydra's heads will regenerate should the player die to it.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Hydras** are minibosses in *Dark Souls*.

title: Hydra
snippet: The Darkroot Basin Hydra can also be approached from the opposite direction, taking the reverse shortcut from Darkroot Garden via the Crest of Artorias door. From this direction, the heads can be eliminated by shooting it with arrows, with the exception of one, drastically reducing the threat of its water projectiles.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : The Hydra is a large sea monster with a body similar to a plesiosaur, but with tentacles underneath a shell-like structure and several long necks and heads. Each head can fire blasts of water from a distance or lunge into the ground for a close range attack.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - ash_lake 
 ash_lake : The Ash Lake Hydra rests near the edge of a sandbar entering the lake. Some distance from the Hydra, a large log lies on top of a ridge of the sandbar. Sheltering behind this log will attract long range attacks from the Hydra, which will be blocked completely by the log. It is possible to shelter behind the log and attack the Hydra safely with a bow; the Hawk Ring and Dragonslayer Greatbow are recommended. When the Hydra is already at very low health, the Symbol of Avarice and Covetous Silver Serpent Ring can be equipped to increase the number of souls gained when the Hydra dies. Equipping the Symbol of Avarice will mean shooting blind, but the Hydra is so large that it is easy to continue hitting its body (it is not necessary or advisable to aim for the heads), for the last few shots required to kill it.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Resting at a bonfire will cause the Hydra to regenerate its lost health, but any heads which have been severed will remain that way.
The Hydra's heads will regenerate should the player die to it.
If one continues through Ash Lake without defeating the Hydra, it will attempt to follow the player. Once the player passes the area where the Giant Clams are, it will leap out of the water and fly across the beach to the other side to continue to pursue the player, bombarding the land below it with water projectiles. It will then follow all the way to the Archtree at the end, making confrontation with the Hydra basically unavoidable.
**If the player attempts to double-back to the entrance to the Ash Lake, the Hydra will once again jump out of the water and fly back over to its original position.
**This is the only time that the Hydra's body can be clearly seen in its entirety.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : The Darkroot Basin Hydra is an easy fight if you do the following: First, you can find a shortcut in Darkroot Garden just east of the Cat Covenant building, keep walking around the northern edge of the garden and you will find a mini gorge path by a lite flower, go right and around the ledge to a ladder. Drop down the ladder to the rope bridge and cross it to the ledge above the Hydra. You can shoot all the heads of the hydra with standard arrows except the last right one. It doesn't take many arrows maybe 100 total for all seven heads. Drop down the ladder to the water level for the last head. Only one head means only one water cannon and it doesn't even come close to hitting you, in fact you have to chase the head when it attacks into the ground. Hit it with any sword a few times and Hydra is toast. It drop a magic sorcery ring and a dragon scale. Have fun

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
If players have given Kaathe the Lordvessel already, then it is possible to prevent Frampt from leaving by rushing around and away from him. As long as he doesn't finish his dialogue, he won't disappear. Players can also prevent him finishing his dialogue by attacking him.
It's actually possible to kill Kingseeker Frampt, but only through the use of third party programs. Frampt has 11,120 HP and drops 5,000 souls after being killed.
Frampt will randomly be found sleeping deeply (usually after resting at a bonfire) even if he was spoken to only moments ago. He can be awoken by attacking him (kicking and punching are sufficient).

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Firelink Shrine, where the pool in front of the decrepit statue used to be. Kingseeker Frampt only appears after the Bells of Awakening have been rung.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine after the player rings both Bells of Awakening. He instructs the player to go to Anor Londo and obtain the Lordvessel. After the player obtains the Lordvessel, Frampt transports them to the entrance of the Kiln of the First Flame, and instructs the player to place the Lordvessel to gain access to the Kiln, and to ultimately kill Gwyn and prolong the Age of Fire.

Should the player give the Lordvessel to Kaathe instead, Frampt will become irate and leave the player for the rest of the playthrough.

title: Unique (upgrade path)
snippet:
Unique (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Unique weapons can be upgraded to +5 down the Unique Path, increasing the weapon's base damage. Unlike standard weapons, unique weapons do not gain an increase in parameter bonus when upgraded.

Most unique weapons cannot be augmented, the exceptions being the Silver Knight Straight Sword and Stone Greataxe.

title: Unique (upgrade path)
snippet:
Unique (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - availability 
 availability : Unique weapons can be upgraded by all blacksmiths, or with the Weapon Smithbox, by using Twinkling Titanite and the required souls.

title: Weapon Modification
snippet:
Weapon Modification -  Dark Souls - mechanic - reinforcement 
 reinforcement : Weapons can be reinforced by any blacksmith NPC, increasing their damage statistics and stability. The player may also do this at any bonfire after purchasing a Weapon Smithbox.

The Weapon Smithbox and all blacksmiths can upgrade any intermediate level of any path not "requiring ascension" (1 to 5, 7 to 10, 12 to 15). To upgrade (on any path) past +5 (to +6) requires a blacksmith. To upgrade (on any path) past +5 (to elemental "+0") requires a blacksmith (see above). To upgrade (on any path) past +10 (to +11) requires a blacksmith. (See the list above if you are unsure of which blacksmith specializes in which elemental qualities.)

The Dragon and Unique upgrade paths are not ascension paths and do not require a specific blacksmith.

title: Weapon Augmentation
snippet:
Weapon Augmentation -  Dark Souls - mechanic - weapons 
 weapons : All Standard, Crystal, and Raw upgrade path can be buffed, with the exception of Bows and Crossbows.

title: Unique (Dark Souls II upgrade path)
snippet:
Unique (Dark Souls II upgrade path) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - upgrading 
 upgrading : Improving these items requires Twinkling Titanite, a rare material that is usually found in a very limited quantity. This makes upgrading unique weapons a very time consuming process.

The main benefit of the upgrade path is that it only requires one type of upgrade material, meaning that farming can be done within one area.

Unique weapons can be upgraded to +5 and it takes 15 Twinkling Titanite to fully upgrade. Armor can also be upgraded to +5 and takes 10 Twinkling Titanite per piece, requiring a total of 40 pieces for a four-piece set.

title: Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path)
snippet:
Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Standard** Reinforcement is a basic form of improving weapons and armor in *Dark Souls II*, that also appeared in *Dark Souls* beforehand. It is independent of the other infusions unlike in *Dark Souls*; you can reinforce an infused weapon, and a reinforced base weapon will not lose its levels from infusion. Also, in contrast to *Dark Souls*, common equipment can be reinforced only up to +10, not +15.

title: Standard (upgrade path)
snippet:
Standard (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Standard upgrades improve the weapon's base damage as well as the scaling it receives from Strength and/or Dexterity, unlike Raw Upgrades. For Strength and Dexterity builds, standard upgrades are the best choice in the long run for this reason. Although the Crystal path technically creates weapons with greater damage output, crystal weapons cannot be repaired and are therefore only effective in the short term; normal weapons can be used indefinitely as long as they are repaired.

All standard weapons (minus certain categories that are never enchantable, such as Bows and Crossbows) may be augmented.

title: Equipment (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Equipment (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - upgrade_materials 
 upgrade_materials : Upgrade Materials are items used to upgrade different types of equipment. All standard weapons and armor are upgraded with Titanite Shards, Large Titanite Shards, Titanite Chunks, and Titante Slabs. Unique weapons and armor are upgraded solely with Twinkling Titanite. Boss weapons are upgraded with Petrified Dragon Bones.

title: Equipment
snippet:
Equipment -  Dark Souls - item - weapons_dark_souls_weapons 
 weapons_dark_souls_weapons : Weapons are equipment that are used primarily to deal damage to enemies. They can attack in either hand, but with a very limited moveset while wielded in the off-hand, and, depending on the weapon type, can also parry or block when in the off-hand. Although with considerably lower damage reduction when compared to shields, blocking can also be achieved when wielding a weapon with two-hands. Most weapons can be upgraded with materials to increase their damage output. Standard weapons can be ascended down various upgrade paths which can alter their base damage, parameter bonus, and in some cases add an elemental damage type and/or auxiliary effect.

title: Weapon Modification
snippet:
Weapon Modification -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : For the equivalent mechanic in Dark Souls II, see Infusion. For the equivalent mechanic in Dark Souls III, see Infusion (Dark Souls III). For the action of the player actively buffing a weapon, see Weapon Augmentation.

**Weapon modification** is a gameplay mechanic of *Dark Souls''.

Weapon modification allows weapons (including shields) to be reinforced in power and/or endowed with special elemental damage, improving their performance against tougher enemies.

title: Weapon Modification
snippet:
Weapon Modification -  Dark Souls - mechanic - ascension 
 ascension : At certain reinforcement levels, specific blacksmiths can ascend a weapon. There are numerous ascension paths to choose from. They can change the stat scaling of the weapon, altering its base statistics dramatically, and sometimes add an elemental damage type and/or an auxiliary effect.

The weapon must be at the required level in order to be upgraded down a specific path and some require specific embers that can be found throughout the world.

title: Armor (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Armor (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - upgrading 
 upgrading : Like weapons, most but not all armor pieces can be upgraded. Armor can be upgraded to +10 or to +5 for those that require Twinkling Titanite. Armor cannot be upgraded down other upgrade paths. Upgraded armor yields higher defensive values and elemental resistance, but never alters Poise.

title: Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path)
snippet:
Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : To reinforce, the player needs an item that is able to be reinforced, the required Titanite and sufficient Souls. For regular titanite weapons, one will need to use 6 Titanite Shards, 6 Large Titanite Shards, 6 Titanite Chunks, and 1 Titanite Slab to ascend a weapon to +10. This can be done through Blacksmith Lenigrast, Steady Hand McDuff, and Weaponsmith Ornifex, however you cannot do it yourself in the fields and labyrinths of Drangleic.

title: Dark (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Dark (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - infusion 
 infusion : Steady Hand McDuff can infuse most weapons with Dark through the use of a Darknight Stone. Once a weapon is infused, the Dark icon () will be displayed next to its image in the HUD.

Uninfused weapons imbued with Dark gain a fixed Dark Damage value (which scales with the Dark Attack Bonus), but the base physical damage is lowered by 30%, as is the base scaling. For example, if a regular weapon that deals 100 physical damage is infused with Dark, its stats switch over to 70 physical damage and 70 Dark Damage.
Weapons with innate Dark Damage gain an additional Dark scaling and a 44% damage increase to Dark, but the base physical damage is lowered by 5%, as is the current scaling.
Armor or shields gain additional Dark resistance while lowering other resistances.

title: Standard (upgrade path)
snippet:
Standard (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : Most weapons can be upgraded on the standard path, but not all. Standard upgrades cannot be performed on weapons which are by default bound to special paths, such as Unique or Dragon weapons, or on (former) standard weapons that have been ascended to another upgrade path. However, a blacksmith can downgrade some ascended weapons back to standard (souls and materials previously expended are permanently lost).

Standard upgrades from +0 to +5 require 9 Titanite Shards (1/1/2/2/3).
Ascension from +5 to +6 requires the Large Ember.
Standard upgrades from +5 to +10 require 9 Large Titanite Shards (1/1/2/2/3).
Ascension from +10 to +11 requires the Very Large Ember.
Standard upgrades from +11 to +14 require 7 Titanite Chunks (1/1/2/3).
Standard upgrade from +14 to +15 requires one Titanite Slab.

title: Magic (upgrade path)
snippet:
Magic (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : By upgrading a weapon down the Magic upgrade path, it gains increased Magic Damage scaling through Intelligence, while also losing Physical Damage through Strength and Dexterity scaling. This makes the Magic path suitable for those with a high Intelligence stat, but low Strength and Dexterity stats.

A standard weapon with a magical weapon augmentation, such as Crystal Magic Weapon, deals more damage than Magic weapons in almost every instance; however, Magic weapons have the advantage of being permanent and not having to be buffed.

The Enchanted upgrade path offers even better scaling with Intelligence than the Magic path, albeit at the cost of even heavier Strength and Dexterity bonus reductions.

title: Attack Rating
snippet:
Attack Rating -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Attack Rating is one of the main factors that determines how much damage weapons do throughout the Dark Souls series.

Attack Rating, commonly abbreviated as AR is a number specific to each Weapon and each element that depends on the weapon, upgrade level, player stats and other equipment that can affect it. This number is used during each attack through a damage formula specific to each game to determine the damage.

title: Titanite Scale
snippet:
Titanite Scale -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Used to reinforce special weapons up to +4. These include all soul-transposed weapons, as well as several otherwise unique weapons.

Reinforcement initially costs only a single Titanite Scale, but doubles in cost for each subsequent level, requiring 8 Titanite Scales to upgrade to +4, and finally a Titanite Slab to upgrade to +5. Fully reinforcing such a weapon requires the use of 15 Titanite Scales and one Titanite Slab. Each level of reinforcement is equal to 2 levels for a weapon upgraded through regular Titanite.
